title: SB175 (2018 Regular): revise certain provisions regarding the carrying of concealed pistols by certain persons.

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (South Dakota) (gun-policy Stage 5, South Dakota); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official South Dakota text (Introduced, 2018-01-31; official copy, https://mylrc.sdlegislature.gov/api/Documents/48220.pdf (sdlegislature.gov DocumentId 48220, BillId 8771))
provenance.note: As filed. No passage vote recorded. Section 2 also rewrites the petty-offense and charge-dismissal wording; Section 4 (SDCL 23-7-8.7) only edits wording and adds a cross-reference to 22-14-9.1.

operative_text:
Section 1 (SDCL 22-14-9): Any person, other than a law enforcement officer as defined in § 22-1-2 acting under color of authority, who: (1) Carries a pistol or revolver, loaded or unloaded, concealed on or about that person's body without a permit issued or recognized as valid under chapter 23-7; or (2) Carries a pistol or revolver, loaded or unloaded, concealed in any vehicle while operating the vehicle, without a permit issued or recognized as valid under chapter 23-7; is guilty of a Class 1 misdemeanor for a first offense. Any second or subsequent violation within ten years of the first violation of the provisions of this section is a Class 6 felony.
Section 2 (SDCL 22-14-9.1): The provisions of § 22-14-9 do not apply to any person who carries a concealed pistol or revolver and also: (1) Carries on or about that person's body a valid South Dakota permit to carry a concealed pistol issued pursuant to chapter 23-7; (2) Carries on or about that person's body a permit recognized as valid pursuant to § 23-7-7.4; or (3) Is a resident of South Dakota who meets the requirements for a temporary permit under § 23-7-7.1 and carries on or about that person's body a valid South Dakota driver license or identification card issued under chapter 32-12.
Section 3 (SDCL 23-7-7): The issuance of a permit to carry a concealed pistol pursuant to the provisions of this chapter does not impose a general prohibition on the carrying of a pistol without a permit by a resident who qualifies under subdivision 22-14-9.1(3).
